name: ftruncate
description: The ftruncate() function truncates the file referenced by the file descriptor to a specified length. If the file is larger than the specified length, the extra data is lost; if shorter, it is extended with null bytes. The file must be open for writing.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to truncate

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: The desired length of the file in bytes

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: fd is not a valid file descriptor
fd is not open for writing
fd does not reference a regular file or a POSIX shared memory object

bugs: A header file bug in glibc 2.12 meant that the minimum value of _POSIX_C_SOURCE required to expose the declaration of ftruncate() was 200809L instead of 200112L, which has been fixed in later glibc versions.
versions: Linux 2.4 added support for large files; original implementation in earlier versions.
